readiness.d: The technology exists and can do it, or one team built it and it works. Not separable from their application, not reusable.
readiness.ev: The application, or the vendor capability

readiness.d: Cleared for enterprise use. Each team assembles the solution itself.
A published standard and an architecture pattern or reference architecture exist.
Reusable building blocks: IaC, security baseline, observability, CI/CD, implementation guidance, support model. Teams self-serve a compliant instance and operate it.
readiness.ev: The module or template repository - a team that used it

readiness.d: An exposed endpoint with a contract. Consumers call it; the platform operates it.
readiness.ev: The endpoint - its service levels - its operational owner - its consumers

consumption.d: EA tells you how to build it.
Reusable modules and components are provided.
A working implementation exists and can be adapted.
The platform provides the underlying infrastructure; the consumer configures on top.
The consumer calls it and gets a result.

generic_assets.d: The institutional standard for how this is built.
Problem, context, forces, solution, resulting context - not just a name.
Change is built and released through a controlled path.
Identity, network and data controls applied by default.
Telemetry emitted without the team adding it.
Operations know what to do when it misbehaves.

realizations.pattern: Internal Foundry deployment standard + agent build standard
realizations.operated: Consumer - each team runs its own instance
realizations.note: Readiness 4 is arguably the correct TARGET here, not a way-station: agents are per-use-case by nature. The improvement path is enriching what comes in the box, not moving to 5.
realizations.notprov: The agent itself: business rules, grounding data, evaluation criteria, human oversight design.

realizations.support: S3.7 Embedding Generation; S3.8 Vector Index Management

realizations.note: THE ROW THAT MATTERS. Nothing enforces entitlements at query time. This is why capability 3.6 can sit at maturity 2 while its headline realization sits at readiness 4. Rows at readiness 0 are the roadmap, and they are the reason the two scales stay separate.

REAL-001.name: Distinct workload identity per instance, not a shared service principal
REAL-001.why: A shared service principal makes every agent's actions indistinguishable. Nothing downstream can attribute or revoke.

REAL-001.name: Automatic registration in the AI system / agent inventory
REAL-001.why: An inventory that depends on teams remembering to register is not an inventory.

REAL-001.name: Tracing and tool-call logging enabled by default
REAL-001.why: If it is not on by default it will not be there when you need to explain what an agent did.

REAL-001.name: Content filtering and safety controls on by default
REAL-001.why: Opt-in safety is the control that is missing exactly when it is needed.

REAL-001.name: Prompt-injection defence configured
REAL-001.why: Content the agent reads can instruct it. Prompt design alone does not stop this at run time.

REAL-001.name: Evaluation harness scaffolded in the template
REAL-001.why: Without a harness in the template, evaluation happens once at launch and never again.

REAL-001.name: Cost attribution tags applied automatically
REAL-001.why: Untagged consumption cannot be attributed, forecast or stopped.

REAL-001.name: A tested way to stop it and revoke its access
REAL-001.why: An untested kill switch is an assumption, not a control.

REAL-001.name: Credential issuance and rotation handled by the platform
REAL-001.why: Credentials created by hand are credentials nobody rotates.

REAL-001.name: Network isolation and private connectivity baseline
REAL-001.why: Isolation applied per team is isolation applied inconsistently.

REAL-001.name: A hook for human approval of consequential actions
REAL-001.why: Oversight designed into the platform is exercised; oversight written into policy is not.

REAL-001.name: Interaction log retention configured to policy
REAL-001.why: Interaction logs are evidence. Retention set per project is evidence you cannot rely on.

REAL-101.name: Entitlement enforced at query time, before ranking
REAL-101.why: Filtering a ranked list after the fact both leaks and distorts relevance. The filter must precede ranking.

REAL-101.name: Citations resolvable to source, version and location
REAL-101.why: A citation that cannot be opened is decoration. It also does not prove the statement is true.

REAL-101.name: Retrieval quality measured against a benchmark
REAL-101.why: Relevance that is never measured degrades silently as the corpus changes.

REAL-101.name: Re-embedding runbook for model change
REAL-101.why: Changing the embedding model invalidates the index. Without a runbook this is an outage.

REAL-101.name: Index residency and access controls enforced
REAL-101.why: A vector index is a copy of the source content, and inherits its residency obligations.
